To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed hybrid thin films comprising ZnO nanowires directly grown on horizontally-aligned carbon nanotube films, which exhibit anisotropic, rapid and high photoconductivity.
we demonstrate a hybrid nanoarchitecture comprising ZnO nanowires (grown on top of) horizontally aligned carbon nanotubes that exhibits rapid and anisotropically enhanced photocurrent response.
the photoconductive response is anisotropic, with the highest gain perpendicular to the Cnt sheet and the highest current parallel to the CNT sheet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of hybrid nanomaterials for applications in opto-electronics, chemical sensing, and energy harvesting.
the design and fabrication of novel hybrid nanostructures that combine the unique properties of different nanomaterials to create a synergistic effect.
the development of new nanocomposites based on carbon nanotubes and other nanostructured materials for applications in energy conversion and storage, optoelectronics and sensing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid nanoarchitecture of ZnO NW arrays on top of a HACNT sheet provides an excellent platform to achieve high photoconductive gain, fast response time, and high photoconductive responsivity.
we demonstrate a rapid and anisotropically photoconductive response in ZnO-coated horizontally aligned carbon nanotubes (CNTs).
this work presents an anisotropic photoactive hybrid material architecture comprising ZnO NWs directly grown on horizontally-aligned carbon nanotubes (CNTs).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a hybrid thin film material system that combines the advantages of both ZnO and CNTs.
we have shown the rapid and anisoropic UV-induced photoconducive response of hybrid thin film comprising ZnO nanowires (ZnO-NWs) directly grown on aligned carbon nanotubes (CNTs) sheets.
we have demonstrated the rapid and anistropic photoconductive response in a hybrid nanoarchitecture comprising ZnO nanowires directly grown on horizontally-aligned CNTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by combining two nanostructured materials, one can achieve a hybrid nanoarchitecture with properties that are not possible with either material alone.
the anisotropic electrical conductivity and morphology of CNTs can be utilized in the design of hybrid nanostructured films to engineer the photoconductive properties of these materials.

the photoresponse of hybrid films comprising vertically oriented nanowires on horizontally aligned carbon nanotubes can be tuned by controlling the morphology of the nanowires and the alignment of the nanotubes, resulting in anisotropic photoresponse and sub-second photoresponse.
